Rashi on Chullin 33b:10:1.hebrew: ונוקמה - למתניתין כר"ע, דהא סתימתאה הוא, ורובא דסתמי אליבא דר"ע, דסתם משנה רבי מאיר וסתם ספרא רבי יהודה וכולהו אליבא דרבי עקיבא, וכיון דשמעת לרבי עקיבא דאמר ידיו תחלות, אוקי למתניתין בדידיה:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:10:1.english: And let us establish it - [Let us establish] the mishna in accordance with R' Akiva, for this is an unattributed teaching, and most unattributed teachings follow R' Akiva's view - for an unattributed mishnah is [the view of] R' Meir, and an unattributed Sifra is [the view of] R' Yehuda, and all of them follow R' Akiva. And since you have heard that R' Akiva says hands are considered a first-degree [source of impurity], establish the mishnah in accordance with him.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:10:2.english: But for chullin, they are seconds - Therefore, [the Gemara] establishes this ruling in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, who states explicitly that even for chullin, they are firsts.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:11:1.english: And let them also be seconds - This is well reconciled according to the view of Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:11:2.english: For we hear him [Rabbi Akiva] say that a second-degree [impurity] makes a third-degree in non-sacred produce (chullin) - Therefore, if blood came out from them [the hands], the hands become disqualified through it.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:12:1.english: As we learned - In the chapter [beginning] "Just as the water..." (Sotah 27b).

Rashi on Chullin 33b:12:2.hebrew: בו ביום - יום שמינו את רבי אלעזר בן עזריה נשיא, וכל היכא דתני בו ביום סתמא, ההוא יומא הוה. והכי אמרינן בברכות (דף כח.): שרץ שנפל לאויר תנור, והרי הוא ראשון, והתנור מטמא מה שבתוכו והוי שני, וכתיב יטמא ומשמע יטמא, אלמא עביד שלישי:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:12:2.english: On that day - The day on which they appointed Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah as Nasi. And wherever [the Mishnah] teaches "on that day" without specification, it was that [same] day. And so we say in Berakhot (page 28a): A creeping animal that fell into the airspace of an oven is [rendered impure in] the first degree, and the oven [in turn] renders impure whatever is inside it, which becomes second degree; and it is written "יטמא" (it shall become impure), which can also be read as "it shall render impure" - proving that it produces a third degree [of impurity].

Rashi on Chullin 33b:12:3.english: Concerning a loaf - Because an ordinary oven typically has loaves inside it.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:12:4.english: That it renders the third [degree of impurity impure] - The verse implies this whether regarding chullin or regarding terumah.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:13:1.english: With Torah-level impurity - Such as [the impurity of] a sheretz (a crawling creature).

Rashi on Chullin 33b:13:2.hebrew: אבל בטומאה דרבנן - כגון ידים, דמדרבנן הוא דהויין שניות:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:13:2.english: But regarding ritual impurity that is [only] rabbinic - Such as [the impurity of unwashed] hands, for it is only by rabbinic decree that they are [considered] secondary [sources of impurity].

Rashi on Chullin 33b:14:1.hebrew: על טהרת הקדש - כגון אדם הרגיל לאכול קדשים, ורוצה להיות רגיל תדיר בשמירת טהרתן, ושומר אף חולין מכל טומאות הפוסלות בקדש, ואשמעינן דשני עביד בהו שלישי:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:14:1.english: For the purity of consecrated food - For example, a person who is accustomed to eating consecrated food and wants to be constantly accustomed to guarding its purity, and so he also guards non-sacred food from all the impurities that disqualify consecrated food. And [the Mishnah] teaches us that a second-degree [impurity] produces in them a third degree [of impurity].

Rashi on Chullin 33b:14:2.hebrew: ודלא כרבי יהושע - דאמר חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקדש לא פסיל בהו שלישי, דבטלה דעתו, ואין יכול להתפיס על חולין טהרת הקדש:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:14:2.english: And not like Rabbi Yehoshua - Who says that with regard to chullin that were made [with the intention of following] the purity level of consecrated food, a third [degree of impurity] does not disqualify them, because his intention is disregarded, and one cannot impose the purity of consecrated food upon chullin.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:14:3.hebrew: האוכל אוכל ראשון - נעשה גופו ראשון להיות מגעו שני, והאוכל אוכל שני נעשה גופו שני להיות מגעו שלישי, והאוכל שלישי, שלישי. ולקמיה מפרש טעמא דר"א דמשוי אוכל כמאכל עצמו. ודוקא שאכל חצי פרס, שזהו שיעור אוכלין טמאין לפסול את הגוייה, והן שתי ביצים, כדאמר בעירובין (דף פב:). אבל בנגיעה לא מטמא אוכל אדם, שאין אדם וכלים מיטמאין אלא מאב הטומאה:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:14:3.english: One who eats first-degree [impure] food - His body becomes [like] a first-degree [source of impurity], so that his touch [conveys] second-degree [impurity]. And one who eats second-degree [impure food], his body becomes second-degree, so that his touch [conveys] third-degree [impurity]. And one who eats third-degree [impure food] [remains only] third-degree [himself, since eating does not advance the degree further]. Further on, [the Gemara] explains the reasoning of Rabbi Elazar, who equates the eater's status with that of the food itself. And this is specifically when he ate a half-loaf [chatzi peras], which is the measure of impure food [required] to disqualify a person's body [from eating terumah] - that being two eggs['-worth] - as is stated in [tractate] Eruvin (82b). But through mere touch, food does not defile a person, for a person or vessels are only rendered impure by a primary source of impurity [an av hatumah].

Rashi on Chullin 33b:15:1.hebrew: רבי יהושע אומר האוכל אוכל ראשון - או אוכל שני הוי שני, דסבירא ליה לרבי יהושע דלא משוינן אוכל כמאכל. ולקמיה מפרש כי אכיל אוכל שני, אמאי משוי ליה שני:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:15:1.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: one who eats first-degree [impure] food - Or, one who eats second-degree food is [himself] second-degree - for Rabbi Yehoshua holds that we do not equate the eater with food [that touches other food, which would decrease by one degree]. And further on, [the Gemara] explains why eating second-degree food renders him second-degree.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:15:2.english: Third [becomes] second with respect to consecrated food - One who eats food of third-degree [impurity], his body becomes second-degree [impure] with respect to consecrated food, and it renders [what it touches] third- and fourth-degree [impure]. Further on, [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:15:3.hebrew: ואין שני לתרומה - דאי נגע לתרומה לא פסל לה, אבל מיכל תרומה אסור, דשלישי מיהא הוי ליאסר באכילה. דאף ע"ג דאמר רבי יהושע אין אוכל נעשה כמאכל, ה"מ באוכל אוכל ראשון דלא הוי ראשון למיעבד שני, אבל לאיתסורי באכילה מודה דשלישי עביד, האוכלו שלישי, וה"נ אמרינן לקמן (חולין דף לד:) בשמעתין:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:15:3.english: And there is no second-degree [impurity] for teruma - For if he touches teruma, he does not disqualify it; but he is forbidden to eat teruma, since he is at least [considered] a third-degree [impurity] with respect to being forbidden to eat. For even though Rabbi Yehoshua said that the eater does not become like the food [he ate], that applies [only] to one who eats first-degree-impure food - that he does not become first-degree himself so as to render [something else] second-degree [by touching it]. But with regard to becoming forbidden to eat, he agrees that a third-degree [status] is created: one who eats it [i.e., the first-degree-impure food] is [deemed] a third-degree [impurity]. And so too we say further on (Chullin 34b) in our discussion.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:16:1.hebrew: בחולין שנעשו על טהרת תרומה - כלומר, האי "אוכל ראשון ושני ושלישי" דקתני בחולין, מיירי במסכת טהרות (פ"ב מ"ב), ובאיזו אוכל חולין אתה מוצא שלישי? הא שני לא עביד שלישי בחולין! אתה מוצאו בחולין שנעשו על טהרת תרומה:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:16:1.english: In chullin that were made according to the purity level of terumah - That is to say, this [Mishnah's] teaching of "one who eats [food that is] first-degree impure, and second-degree, and third-degree" with regard to chullin is discussed in Tractate Taharot (2:2). And in what case of eating chullin do you find a third-degree [impurity]? A second-degree [impure item] does not make a third-degree in chullin! You find it [only] in chullin that were made according to the purity level of terumah.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:17:1.hebrew: על טהרת תרומה אין על טהרת הקדש לא - דבטלה דעתו, ואין שם טהרת הקדש נתפסת עליהם, אבל בטהרת תרומה נתפסין. אלמא מתניתין דלא כרבי יהושע, אבל כר"א אתיא, דהא סתם קאמר שלישי שלישי, אפילו בחולין שנעשו על טהרת הקדש:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:17:1.english: On the purity level of terumah, yes; on the purity level of consecrated food, no - Because his intention is nullified, and the status of "purity of consecrated food" does not take hold on them; but with "purity of terumah" it does take hold. Evidently the mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua, but it accords with Rabbi Eliezer, since he states unqualifiedly, "third-degree [impurity disqualifies], third-degree," even in the case of chullin that were treated with the stringency of consecrated food's purity.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:1:1.hebrew: כל הטעון ביאת מים מדברי סופרים - כל שהוא מן התורה טהור, וסופרים גזרו עליו טומאה, כגון הידים והכלים שנטמאו במשקין, והבא ראשו ורובו במים שאובין, וכל האמורים ביציאות השבת אצל שמונה עשר דבר - כולם טומאת שני לטומאה גזרו עליהם, ומטמא את הקדש עד שעושהו שלישי, וטמא הוא שעושה רביעי:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:1:1.english: Anything requiring immersion in water by rabbinic decree - Anything that is pure according to the Torah, but the Sages decreed impurity upon it - such as hands and vessels that became impure through liquids, one who immersed his head and most of his body in drawn water, and all those enumerated in [the mishna of] "the departures of Shabbat," among the eighteen things - for all of these, [the Sages] decreed upon them the status of a second degree of impurity; it renders consecrated items impure until it makes them a third degree, and that [third-degree item] is impure in that it makes a fourth degree.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:1:2.hebrew: ופוסל את התרומה - דשלישי בתרומה פסול, ולא עביד רביעי. במסכת סוטה נפקא לן מטבול יום, בקל וחומר:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:1:2.english: And it renders terumah invalid - For [a food] that is third-degree [in impurity] with regard to terumah is invalid, but it does not produce a fourth degree. In tractate Sotah this is derived with regard to one who immersed that day (a tevul yom), by means of a kal vachomer (an a fortiori inference).

Rashi on Chullin 33b:2:1.english: And the Sages prohibit [it] with regard to tithe - This shows that tithe is different from ordinary [non-sacred] produce.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:3:1.english: From where? - You derived it from the rabbinic law that [a food of] second-degree [impurity] renders [another food] third-degree, with regard to tithe (ma'aser).

Rashi on Chullin 33b:3:2.hebrew: דלמא עד כאן - לא קאסרי רבנן אלא דאסור לאכול מי שידיו מסואבות, או הבא במים שאובים, לא יאכל במעשר, דאסורין במעשר אכילה משמע, אבל באכילה דחולין מודו, ובנגיעה דמעשר נמי לא אסרי, ומתניתין אסר להו אפילו בנגיעה:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:3:2.english: Perhaps [only] until here - The Rabbis prohibited only that one whose hands are unclean, or one who came into contact with drawn water, may not eat of ma'aser, for [the expression] "forbidden with respect to ma'aser" implies [only] eating; but with respect to eating chullin, they concede [it is permitted], and they likewise do not forbid touching ma'aser; whereas our mishnah forbids them even by touching.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:4:1.hebrew: מדקתני נאכלין - ולא קתני אוכלין מי שידיו מסואבות, דנידוק מינה הא יצא דם לא יאכלם, אלא נאכלין לאחרים על ידי מי שידיו מסואבות:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:4:1.english: Since it teaches "are eaten" - and does not teach "one whose hands are soiled eats [them]," for [had it said so] we would infer from it that once blood has come out [of the carcass, rendering it fit to receive impurity], he may not eat it. Rather, [it teaches] "are eaten" - meaning, by others, through the agency of one whose hands are soiled.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:4:2.hebrew: דקספי ליה חבריה - ובהא דייקינן: הא הוכשרו אין נאכלין לאחרים, אלמא פסלא בהו נגיעת שני, והא ליכא למאן דאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:4:2.english: That his fellow fed him - And from this we infer precisely: If they had been rendered susceptible [to impurity, by contact with liquid], they may not be eaten by [being fed to] others, which shows that the contact of one with second-degree impurity disqualifies them. But there is no one who holds this.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:4:3.hebrew: מי לא עסקינן כו' - כלומר, מי לא משמע נמי נאכלין לאחרים, ואפילו הכי דייק מתניתין: הא יצא מהן דם אין נאכלין:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:4:3.english: Are we not dealing, etc. - That is to say, does [the wording] "they are eaten" not also imply "eaten by others" [i.e., that another person feeds it to him], and even so the mishna precisely infers: If blood emerged from them, they are not eaten.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:5:1.hebrew: הכא - מתניתין דדייק הא הוכשרו פסלא בהו נגיעת ידים מסואבות, לאו בידים שניות קאמר, אלא בידים תחלות, ולקמיה מפרש הי נינהו ידים תחלות, ומתניתין דקאמר דידים תחלות הוזכרו אף להיות ראשונות לחולין, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר היא:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:5:1.english: Here - The Mishnah which infers, "Indeed, they were rendered susceptible [to impurity, and] the touch of unclean hands invalidates them," is not speaking of hands [defiled] in the second degree, but rather of hands [defiled] in the first degree; and further on, [the Gemara] will explain which are considered hands of the first degree. And the Mishnah which states that hands of the first degree are mentioned even so as to be a first-degree [source of impurity] for chullin, is [the view of] Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:5:2.hebrew: דתניא אין ידים תחלות לחולין - במקום שהוזכר ידים תחלות, כגון ידים שהוכנסו לבית המנוגע דמיקרו תחלות, לא הוזכרו אצל חולין, דבחולין לא הוו אלא שניות, אלא לענין תרומה וקדשים שווינהו תחלות, משא"כ בשאר ידים דאפילו לתרומה שניות הויין:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:5:2.english: As it was taught: Hands are not [considered] first-degree [impure] with respect to chullin - Wherever hands are mentioned as first-degree, such as hands that were brought into a house afflicted with tzaraat, which are termed first-degree, this was not mentioned with respect to chullin, for with chullin they are only second-degree. Rather, only with regard to terumah and consecrated items did [the Sages] render them first-degree - unlike other [causes of impurity to] hands, which are second-degree even with regard to terumah.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:5:3.hebrew: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר אומר ידים תחלות - הוזכרו אצל חולין, וידים שניות כגון סתם ידים הוזכרו אצל תרומה, לעשותה שלישי ולפוסלה:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:5:3.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: hands are first-degree [impure] - This was stated with regard to chullin. And [the concept of] "hands are second-degree," such as ordinary [unwashed] hands, was stated with regard to terumah, to render it third-degree and thereby disqualify it.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:7:1.english: He inserted his hands - [This is referring to a case] when he washed them and purified them from the impurity of hands with unknown [i.e., unwashed] status.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:8:1.hebrew: ביאה במקצת לא שמה ביאה - דאי שמה ביאה הוי כל גופו טמא ובעי טבילה משום והבא אל הבית (ויקרא יד), ואנן ידים הוא דמטמינן. וטעמא דתרוייהו משום דגזרו ידיו אטו ביאת כל גופו, ובההיא גזרה פליגי איזו טומאה גזרו על ידיו: ר"ע סבר ידיו גזרו רבנן שיהו תחלות כגופו אם נכנס שם, דהוי ראשון מדאורייתא:
Rashi on Chullin 33b:8:1.english: Partial entry is not called entry - For if it were called entry, his entire body would become impure and he would need immersion, because of "and he who enters the house" (Leviticus 14); but we [only] render his hands impure. And the reason for both [rulings] is that they decreed [impurity] upon the hands on account of the entry of the whole body, and it is about that very decree that they disagree as to what [level of] impurity they decreed upon the hands: R. Akiva holds that the Sages decreed concerning the hands that they should be sources of impurity, like [what would happen to] the body if it had entered there - which would be a primary degree of impurity by Torah law.

Rashi on Chullin 33b:9:1.english: Like ordinary hands - And the practical difference is that even if he washed them and immediately inserted them, without touching anything, they would be of second-degree [impurity] due to the insertion.

Tosafot on Chullin 33b:13:1.hebrew: הני מילי בטומאה דאורייתא אבל בטומאה דרבנן לא - תימה, דבפרק ה' דסוטה (דף ל.) א"ר אסי: רבי מאיר ורבי יהושע סברי אין שני עושה שלישי בחולין; רבי מאיר, דתנן: כל הטעון ביאת מים מדברי סופרים כו' ומותר בחולין. ומאי ראיה מייתי מיניה? הא רבי עקיבא מודה בטומאה דרבנן, כדאמר הכא, דמשמע דאתא לאפוקי מדר' עקיבא, דאמר התם לעיל שני עושה שלישי בחולין. וי"ל דרבי אסי לית ליה דיחוי דהכא, והשתא לרבי אסי ההיא דפרק קמא דשבת (דף יג:) דאלו פוסלין את התרומה, דמשמע תרומה ולא חולין, אתא דלא כר"ע, דאפילו בטומאה דרבנן סבר דשני עושה שלישי בחולין:
Tosafot on Chullin 33b:13:1.english: This applies only to Torah-level impurity, but not to rabbinic impurity - This is difficult, for in the fifth chapter of Sotah (30a), R. Assi said: R. Meir and R. Yehoshua hold that a [thing of] second-degree [impurity] does not render [another thing] third-degree in chullin (non-sacred food) — [this follows] R. Meir, as we learned: "Whatever requires immersion in water by rabbinic decree, etc., is permitted in chullin." But what proof does he bring from this? Does not R. Akiva also concede regarding rabbinic impurity, as is stated here, which implies that [the Mishnah] comes to exclude [only] from R. Akiva's view — who held there, earlier, that a second degree renders a third degree in chullin? And one can say that R. Assi does not accept the [concept of] dichuy (deferral/exclusion) [as applied] here. And now, according to R. Assi, that [passage] in the first chapter of Shabbat (13b), "these invalidate terumah" — which implies terumah but not chullin — comes to teach [the law] not in accordance with R. Akiva, who held that even regarding rabbinic impurity, a second degree renders a third degree in chullin.

Tosafot on Chullin 33b:14:1.hebrew: האוכל אוכל ראשון ראשון - בפ"ק דשבת (דף יד.) מפרש טעמא, משום דזימנין דאכיל אוכלין טמאים ושקיל משקין דתרומה ושדי בפומיה. וא"ת: ואמאי הוי ראשון? בשני סגי! וכ"ת משום מעשר שני דאין שני פוסלו, והלא אפילו משקים חולין נעשים ראשונים על ידי שני! ויש לומר דרבי אליעזר משוה מדותיו, לעשות אוכל כמאכל לגמרי:
Tosafot on Chullin 33b:14:1.english: One who eats first-degree [impure] food becomes first-degree - In the first chapter of Shabbat (14a) the reason is explained: because sometimes he eats impure foods and [then] takes liquids of terumah and puts [them] into his mouth. And if you ask: why should he become first-degree? Second-degree should suffice! And if you say [the reason is] on account of second tithe (ma'aser sheni), since second-degree [impurity] does not disqualify it - but even ordinary (chullin) liquids become first-degree through [contact with] second-degree [impurity]! One can answer that Rabbi Eliezer equalizes his measures, to make the eater [equivalent] to the food he ate, entirely.

Tosafot on Chullin 33b:3:1.hebrew: ודלמא עד כאן לא פליגי אלא באכילה - אע"ג דנקט לשון "דלמא", נראה שכן הוא האמת, וברייתא מוכחת כן: דאסורין במעשר משמע באכילה. ובפרק חומר בקדש (חגיגה דף יח:) לא גריס "ודלמא" בשום ספר:
Tosafot on Chullin 33b:3:1.english: But perhaps until here they only disagree with regard to eating - Even though [the Gemara] employs the term "perhaps" (dilma), it appears that this is indeed correct, and a beraita proves it: [the fact that they are] "forbidden with respect to tithe (ma'aser)" implies with respect to eating. And in Perek Chomer BaKodesh (Chagigah 18b), the word "ve-dilma" is not found in the text of any manuscript.

Tosafot on Chullin 33b:3:2.hebrew: ובאכילה דחולין לא פליגי - לא היה צריך כאן לאכילה דחולין, אלא אגב דנקטיה במס' חגיגה (ג"ז שם), נקטיה הכא:
Tosafot on Chullin 33b:3:2.english: And they do not disagree about eating chullin - There was no need here [to mention] eating of chullin; rather, since it was stated in tractate Chagigah (this too, there), it was stated here as well.

Tosafot on Chullin 33b:4:1.hebrew: והא נגיעה היא מדקתני ונאכלין - וא"ת: ואפילו אם היה תנן אוכלין, יכול לדקדק דבנגיעה איירי, דאי בנגיעה שרי, אמאי לא יאכל כשיצא מהן דם, כיון דאין גופו טמא ומותר ליגע? ויש לומר, דהחמירו חכמים שלא לאכול כשיש לו ידים מסואבות, אף על גב דמותר ליגע:
Tosafot on Chullin 33b:4:1.english: But surely it is touching, since it teaches: "and they are eaten" - And if you should say: even had it taught "they eat" (okhlin), one could still infer precisely that it deals with touching, for if touching were permitted, why should he not eat when blood came out from them (his hands), since his body is not impure and he is permitted to touch [with them]? - One can say that the Sages were stringent not to eat when one has soiled hands, even though he is permitted to touch [with them].

Tosafot on Chullin 33b:8:1.hebrew: דכולי עלמא ביאה במקצת לא שמה ביאה - ואפילו לריש לקיש דאמר (זבחים דף לב:) טמא שהכניס ידו לפנים לוקה, היינו דוקא במקדש, דדרשינן מדכתיב בכל קדש לא תגע ואל המקדש לא תבא עד מלאת ימי טהרה, מה נגיעה במקצת שמה נגיעה, אף ביאה במקצת במקדש שמה ביאה:
Tosafot on Chullin 33b:8:1.english: According to everyone, a partial entry is not called an entry - And even according to Reish Lakish, who says (Zevachim 32b) that a tamei person who inserted his hand inward [into the Sanctuary] is liable to lashes, that is specifically with regard to the Temple, for we derive [it] from that which is written, "You shall not touch any holy thing, and you shall not come into the Sanctuary, until the days of your purification are fulfilled": just as partial touching is called touching, so too a partial entry into the Temple is called an entry.
